name: Three-Vertex Directed-Path Coefficient Restriction
definition: In the oriented bipartite-graph construction, take the directed path $P:v_0\to v_1\to v_2$. Let $B=C(P)$ and let $D=C(\{v_0,v_2\})$ be the zero section obtained by removing the private middle vertex. Restrict the coefficient rows of $B$ to the three rows of $D$.
properties: $B$ has 31 concepts and $D$ has 22. Both coefficient spaces are contractible and the restriction is an open surjection, but its fibers vary across two monomial walls: the fiber has two contractible components when both endpoint log differences are nonpositive and is contractible otherwise.
